history.summary: RELATED RECORD: these twelve shrines are part of the Dakshineswar Kali Temple complex - seq 2470 (id dakshineswar-kali-temple). Kept as a separate record per CSV row 2471. Built by Rani Rashmoni on the Hooghly riverfront flanking the main ghat: twelve identical shrines in two rows of six, in the traditional Bengali aat-chala (eight-roofed) style, each housing a Shiva lingam and facing east. Local tradition calls them the twelve jyotirlingams. Their consecration is dated with the main complex's installation ceremony of 31 May 1855.

name: Dwadash Shiva Mandir (Twelve Shiva Temples)
town_description: Dakshineswar is a historic locality in Kamarhati municipality, North 24 Parganas, on the eastern bank of the Hooghly river, within Greater Kolkata. It is famed for the Kali temple and as the 19th-century home of the mystic Ramakrishna.
